findings.title: Missing HTTP Security Defense-in-Depth Headers
findings.description: The application fails to set important HTTP security headers: Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Strict-Transport-Security.
findings.evidence: HTTP response headers received: {'X-Powered-By': 'Express', 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*', 'Accept-Ranges': 'bytes', 'Cache-Control': 'public, max-age=0', 'Last-Modified': 'Tue, 28 Jul 2026 10:36:19 GMT', 'ETag': 'W/"3cc5-19fa84bf942"', 'Content-Type': 'text/html; charset=UTF-8', 'Content-Length': '15557', 'Date': 'Tue, 28 Jul 2026 10:41:25 GMT', 'Connection': 'keep-alive', 'Keep-Alive': 'timeout=5'}
findings.remediation: Configure helmet.js or Express middleware to enforce Content-Security-Policy, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, and X-Content-Type-Options.

findings.title: Permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) Policy
findings.description: The API allows requests from arbitrary origins ('*'), exposing sensitive data to cross-origin reads if cookies/tokens are added.
findings.remediation: Restrict CORS to trusted admin domain origins instead of wildcard '*'.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Admin Write Access on Sensitive Endpoint
findings.description: Any unauthenticated attacker can submit POST requests to /api/v1/proxies/add and inject arbitrary proxy nodes into the active database without authorization.
findings.remediation: Enforce mandatory API Key authentication (e.g. Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>) on all administrative POST/DELETE endpoints.

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via Unvalidated URL Input
findings.description: The proxy registration endpoint accepts internal IP addresses (e.g., 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1) and non-HTTP protocols without strict URL validation.
findings.evidence: Submitted SSRF payloads ['http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/', 'http://127.0.0.1:22/', 'file:///etc/passwd'] -> Server responded with success: {"success":true,"addedCount":0,"totalPoolSize":15}
findings.remediation: Validate URL hostname against RFC 1918 private address ranges and enforce only public 'http://', 'https://', 'socks4://', and 'socks5://' schemes.

findings.title: Unthrottled Resource-Intensive Sweep Causes Server Timeout (DoS Risk)
findings.description: Sending concurrent POST requests to /api/v1/proxies/check caused the Node.js server event loop to stall and time out, confirming susceptibility to Denial of Service (DoS).
findings.evidence: HTTPConnectionPool read timeout after rapid concurrent sweep trigger requests.
findings.remediation: Add express-rate-limit and debouncing logic so runPoolSweep() cannot be executed concurrently.
